The Hot Rod Magazine is an esteemed American publication that focuses on hot rod modifications, drag racing, and muscle cars. It has been in circulation since its inception in January 1948, making it the longest-running magazine dedicated to these automotive pursuits.

Robert E. Petersen played a pivotal role in establishing this influential publication. He founded the magazine and established Petersen Publishing Company, which remains the primary publisher today. The inaugural editor of the Hot Rod Magazine was Wally Parks, whose contributions extended beyond just founding the magazine; he also co-founded the National Hot Rod Association (NHRA).

In 1998, Petersen Publishing was acquired by British publisher EMAP, followed by a subsequent sale to Primedia in 2001. Since then, the magazine continues to thrive under the current ownership structure, maintaining its status as a leading source for enthusiasts interested in modifying and enhancing their vehicles for both performance and aesthetics.
